ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: The Bode plot of a transfer function \(G(s)\) is shown in the figure. The gain \(20\log |G(s)|\) is 32 dB at 1 rad/s and -8 dB at 10 rad/s. The phase is negative for all \(\omega\). Determine \(G(s)\).
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure is the Bode magnitude-frequency plot of G(s), the vertical axis is Gain(dB), the horizontal axis is angular frequency omega(rad/s), and the horizontal axis is marked with 1, 10, and 100. The magnitude curve is a straight line that decreases as frequency increases; at omega = 1 rad/s the gain is about 32 dB, at omega = 10 rad/s it passes near -8 dB, and the figure also has a dashed-line annotation corresponding to -8 dB. The problem also gives that the phase is negative for all omega. Reasoning: From 1 rad/s to 10 rad/s is one decade, and the gain changes from 32 dB to -8 dB, so the slope is (-8 - 32)/(log10(10) - log10(1)) = -40 dB/decade. A Bode magnitude-frequency slope of -40 dB/decade corresponds to two integrator links, so the transfer function form is G(s) = K/s^2. Using the magnitude at omega = 1 rad/s: |G(j1)| = K/1^2 = K, and 20 log10 K = 32, so K = 10^(32/20) = 10^1.6 ≈ 39.8. Positive K together with two integrator links can have phase -180 degrees, satisfying that the phase is negative for all omega. Therefore G(s) = 39.8/s^2.

raw_record.question_text: The Bode plot of a transfer function \(G(s)\) is shown in the figure. The gain \(20\log |G(s)|\) is 32 dB at 1 rad/s and -8 dB at 10 rad/s. The phase is negative for all \(\omega\). Determine \(G(s)\).

method.method_draft: First describe the plot: the gain line falls from 32 dB at 1 rad/s to -8 dB at 10 rad/s, giving slope (-8 - 32)/(log10 10 - log10 1) = -40 dB/decade. Apply Bode slope rules to identify two integrators, so G(s) must be K/s^2. Use the point at ω = 1: 20 log10 |G(j1)| = 20 log10 K = 32, hence K ≈ 39.8. The given negative phase condition selects the positive K two-integrator form rather than a numerator/differentiator alternative. Conclude G(s)=39.8/s^2.
